clue.text: Disturbance involving soldiers in early stage of parachute jump

indicators.note: the jump phrase involves, or wraps round, the word for soldiers

parts.note: free fall is the drop before the canopy opens
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Some trouble breaks out among troops just as they leap from the plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl or melee in which everyone joins is a general disturbance.

clue.text: A lover's intense passion

explanation.surface: A lover feels a burning desire.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former sweetheart, and a fire of feeling is ardent emotion.

clue.text: Led up between sheep, one's entered the plant

indicators.note: the word for one's goes into the rest
the turned word sits between the letters of the sheep

parts.note: ewes are female sheep

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
I for one, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone led uphill among the flock finds an Alpine flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led up' reads as being guided uphill, but in a down clue 'up' turns the word over to give DEL; 'between' and 'entered' are the two container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white-flowered mountain plant of the Alps.

clue.text: Simile, say, for celebrity from public address

parts.note: a public figure is a celebrity
of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
a speech is an address given in public

explanation.surface: A comparison is used by a famous person speaking in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is one example of a rhetorical device.

clue.text: New Lord President describing a staff of office

indicators.note: new letters means the word is remade in a fresh order

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A newly made peer becomes president and carries a ceremonial staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff of office is a rod, so the adjective means resembling one.

clue.text: Brief reason against appearing in non-clerical garb

indicators.note: the argument against shows up inside the lay word
the lay word clothes the argument against it

parts.note: laic means lay, not of the clergy
a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A short argument against a priest turning up out of uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse, concise reply uses few words, like the Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: Noisy American's sustained protest

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
US for American, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A loud American keeps up a long complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolonged complaint or commotion is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Speak about territory only partly utilized

annotationWithheld.why: Speak about territory only partly utilized (5): UTTER, but no parse found gives 'about' a job; UT and TER would need 'only partly' to work on both words at once
annotationWithheld.clue: Speak about territory only partly utilized

clue.text: Desire for Tennessee's public transport?

parts.note: Tennessee Williams wrote a play whose title names a tram called Desire

explanation.surface: A longing for buses in the state of Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennessee is not the state but the playwright Tennessee Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram running on city rails is an American form of public transport.

clue.text: They make good army couples, supporting athletic activity

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece is placed below the other

parts.note: running is an athletic activity
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
pairs are couples

explanation.surface: Soldiers in pairs back up a sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs carried out as needed are fixes that set things right again.

clue.text: Got satisfaction for archdeacon in antiquated accommodation

indicators.note: the archdeacon's title sits in the word for old
the word for old provides room for the archdeacon's title

parts.note: aged means old or antiquated
Ven, the Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A senior cleric is compensated for being housed in an old building.
explanation.definitionFit: To get revenge for a wrong is to obtain satisfaction for it.

clue.text: Bar used by players on board?

explanation.surface: A pub's bar is used by people playing a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or pub bar is a serving top, and a draught or ludo piece is a token moved on a board.

clue.text: Get injured and die restraining hostilities of 1901-10

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the word for fighting within them
injured letters are damaged and rearranged

parts.note: war means hostilities

explanation.surface: A soldier is wounded and killed in a war in the early twentieth century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' scrambles AND DIE into EDDIAN, and 'restraining' puts WAR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward VII reigned 1901-10, so that decade's period takes his name.

clue.text: The language of a senor when intoxicated!

indicators.note: a drunk word is staggered into a new order of letters

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman, once drunk, speaks a strange tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the tongue of medieval Scandinavia.

clue.text: Leave no capital

parts.note: to quit is to leave
O is nought or nothing, a zero meaning no

explanation.surface: No holiday is allowed for a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Quito is the capital city of Ecuador.

clue.text: Quiet pun Head of Literature made, describing Anna's towns

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement
the head of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A quiet joke made by a literature professor about a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Bennett's novel Anna of the Five Towns is set in the Staffordshire Potteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Bennett's Anna has five towns, and fivefold is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Odd fish in the Cam — with small head!

explanation.surface: A strange fish swims in Cambridge's river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam looks like the Cambridge river; with a small head, a lower-case c, it is a cam, a rotating engine part also called an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd fish is a strange person, and in engineering an off-centre disc driving a rod is a kind of cam.

clue.text: Maiden in port takes part in complicated procedure

indicators.note: the maiden letter goes inside the port

parts.note: Riga is the Latvian port and capital
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A young woman in a harbour town takes a role in a tangled affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-winded, fussy process is a palaver or rigmarole.

clue.text: Demanding little sibling in goal

indicators.note: the sibling sits inside the word for aim

parts.note: intent means aim or goal
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A younger sister keeps pushing to go in goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone persistent and pressing is exacting or demanding.

clue.text: Went out to smother politician, being provoked

indicators.note: the word for went out covers the politician inside it

parts.note: exited means went out
C stands for Conservative, a British party politician

explanation.surface: Someone left in order to stifle a politician, having been goaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred up or aroused is the state of someone being provoked.

clue.text: Tiptop island with a lake that is warm

parts.note: the top of the word tip is its first letter, T
Herm is one of the Channel Islands
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A first-rate island with a lake has a mild climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal clothing or springs give heat, so the word means warm.

clue.text: He backs another man with gold

indicators.note: backs means the man's name and the gold are read in reverse order of letters

parts.note: Reg is a man's name
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A man supports a friend with a gift of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reverses REG plus OR to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is a male name, so it can stand for a man referred to as he.

clue.text: Commercial customers raise the wind

explanation.surface: Shoppers stir up a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' only links the two senses; the trades are the steady tropical winds.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm selling to the trade serves business buyers, and a trade is a steady tropical wind.

clue.text: Legendary supporter cut down in the end

indicators.note: cut down means the phrase is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: at last means in the end

explanation.surface: A mythical backer is finally felled.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titan Atlas held up the heavens on his shoulders.

clue.text: Inferior headgear worn by male sailor

indicators.note: the cap is worn round the male pronoun, which goes inside it

parts.note: a cap is headgear
he is the male pronoun
Jack, as in Jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor wears a shabby hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapjack seller offers shoddy goods, so the word means poor or inferior.

clue.text: Student in Kent irregularly made obeisance

indicators.note: the student letter goes inside the rearranged county
irregularly means the letters are set out of order

parts.note: L is a learner, the letter on a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student in Kent bowed at odd times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregularly' turns KENT into KNET; Kent is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on one's knees is a gesture of homage or obeisance.

clue.text: European jazz fan is a skunk when in America!

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
cat is jazz slang for an aficionado

explanation.surface: A jazz lover from Europe turns out to be a stinker in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the polecat name is given to the skunk.

clue.text: Old coin found by me, an illustrator in France

parts.note: moi is French for me, the French flavour set by 'in France'
Gustave Doré was a French illustrator

explanation.surface: A French artist and I come across an antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The moidore was a Portuguese gold piece once current in Britain.

clue.text: Rugby schoolboy misses beginning of blow-out

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a big meal is dropped

parts.note: a blow-out is a lavish meal, a feast

explanation.surface: A pupil at Rugby skips the start of a big dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is an English public school; Harry East is Tom's friend in Tom Brown's School Days, set there.
explanation.definitionFit: East is a pupil at Rugby School in Thomas Hughes's novel.

clue.text: Youth's rise restricts state benefit

indicators.note: the word for rise confines the welfare payment inside it

parts.note: an ascent is a rise
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A young person's pay increase limits their welfare payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager, between child and adult, is a youth.
